setting.placeName:
Legation of the United States,
St. Petersburg

opener.dateline:
Legation of the United States,
St. Petersburg, August 8–20, 1872.

div.p: The undersigned, chargé d’affaires of the United States of America, has the honor to inform his excellency, Mr. de Westmann, privy councilor, acting minister of foreign affairs, &c, that he has received the instruction of the President to call the attention of the imperial government to the condition of the Hebrews in Roumania.

The persecutions which the Hebrews in the principalities have undergone and are undergoing are so notorious that this grievance assumes as it were a cosmopolitan character, in the redress of which all countries, governments, and creeds are alike interested. The Government of the United States was not a party to the convention of Paris of 1858, of which the acts complained of by the Hebrews seem clearly an infraction, and, as a rule, scrupulously abstains from interfering in the public affairs of other countries, yet the persecution of a people for their race or religion cannot fail to evoke for them the sympathies of the American people.

The Government of the United States thinks that if the imperial government were informed of the sympathy felt in America for the persecuted and outraged Hebrews of the principalities, the imperial government might feel encouraged in the efforts they are making to redress the grievances complained of.

If the imperial government should be able, either alone or in conjunction with the other European governments which signed the convention of Paris, to alleviate the condition of the Roumanian Hebrews, they would be assured of the lively gratitude and sympathy of the Government and people of the United States.
The undersigned takes this occasion to renew to his excellency the assurances of his high esteem and profound consideration.
